This checklist covers the contacts, forms, and procedures for several major Long Beach facilities. For firms carrying high PI volume,[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered retrieval reporting an average turnaround of a couple of weeks rather than the longer timelines manual retrieval can produce, with validation that catches authorization errors before they cause rejections.

## **Understanding Medical Records Requests for Personal Injury Cases**


### **Why Medical Records Are Crucial in PI Claims**


Medical records often form a central part of the evidentiary foundation in personal injury cases. They establish the causal link between the incident and the injuries, quantify damages, and give experts the clinical detail they need.


Long Beach spreads that work across several hospital systems, urgent care networks, a VA medical center, and specialty clinics, each with its own procedures, forms, and timelines. Retrieval across providers for one client eats real paralegal hours.


Documents that matter most in a PI file:


-


Emergency department and triage notes


-


Imaging studies on disc or digital


-


Operative reports and surgical notes


-


Discharge summaries and follow-up instructions


-


Billing records for damages


-


Physical therapy progress notes


-


Specialist consultations


### **Common Challenges in Medical Record Acquisition**


Provider response times vary widely, and authorization requirements differ between systems, so a form that clears MemorialCare may come back from Dignity Health. The most frequent causes of delay:


-


Missing signatures


-


Incomplete date ranges that omit relevant treatment periods


-


Unchecked selections for specially protected record categories


-


Misspelled names or wrong dates of birth


-


Outdated forms


-


Wrong department submissions routed to billing instead of HIM


## **Navigating HIPAA and Essential Medical Records Release Forms**


### **Key Elements of a Valid HIPAA Authorization**


A HIPAA-compliant authorization must contain specific elements to be valid under[federal law](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/index.html) . Missing one gives providers grounds to reject the request.


The federally required elements are:


-


**Description of information** : A meaningful description of the records


-


**Disclosing party** : Identification of the person or entity authorized to make the disclosure


-


**Recipient identification** : Identification of who may receive the information


-


**Purpose statement** : The reason for the disclosure


-


**Expiration** : A specific date or event that terminates the authorization


-


**Patient signature and date** : Handwritten or valid electronic signature with execution date


-


**Required notices** : Including the patient's right to revoke in writing


Providers commonly also ask for date of birth, address, and other identifiers. Those help match records but are not federal core elements, so do not treat a facility's identification fields and HIPAA's requirements as the same list.


For specially protected categories, the statutory form in Evidence Code § 1158 separately calls out mental health records, alcohol or drug records, and HIV test results, so make those selections deliberately. Substance use disorder records held by a qualifying program may also fall under 42 CFR Part 2, whose revised requirements became mandatory in February 2026. Other federal or state confidentiality rules can apply depending on the record.


### **Where to Find and Customize Release Forms**


Each Long Beach system publishes its own authorization forms. Evidence Code § 1158 also provides that a provider shall accept a signed and completed authorization substantially in the statutory form where the provider determines it is valid and it meets the formatting requirement.


**Facility-specific forms:**


-


**MemorialCare** : Available on the[MemorialCare records page](https://www.memorialcare.org/patients-visitors/medical-records-forms) , covering system facilities including Miller Children's Hospital


-


**VA Long Beach** :[VA Form 10-5345a](https://www.va.gov/find-forms/) for an individual's own records, and VA Form 10-5345 to authorize disclosure to a third party such as a law firm


-


**St. Mary Medical Center** : Available through the HIM department at (562) 491-9941 or from[CommonSpirit patient resources](https://www.commonspirit.org/patient-resources)


-


**LA County facilities** : Available from[LA County DHS](https://dhs.lacounty.gov/)

## **Collecting Old Medical Records: Strategies and Resources**


### **Tips for Locating Records from Closed Practices**


Physicians retire, practices close, systems merge. California retention requirements vary by provider and record type. For general acute care hospitals, Title 22 CCR § 70751 requires records to be preserved for at least seven years after discharge, with a separate rule for minors. Strategies for finding them:


-


**Check Medical Board guidance** : Physicians closing a practice must tell patients where records will be stored, but California has no central repository for medical records


-


**Check with successor practices** : When practices merge or are acquired, the acquiring entity typically assumes custody


-


**Search state licensing databases** : Confirm whether a provider is still licensed and where


-


**Review hospital affiliations** : Physicians with privileges may have duplicate records in the hospital system


-


**Check county health departments** : For closed community health centers, counties sometimes assume custody

## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Do When Records Are Missing**

-


All specified record types


-


Operative reports for surgeries referenced in the notes


-


Discharge summaries for every hospitalization


-

-


Physical therapy notes covering the treatment period

## **California Fees and Timing: Know Which Pathway Applies**


The most common mistake in a California records checklist is treating patient access law and attorney prelitigation law as the same thing.


Patient and personal representative requests fall under[Health and Safety Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSS&sectionNum=123110) § 123110. Providers may charge a reasonable, cost-based fee for paper or electronic copies, subject to statutory limits: $0.25 per page for paper, or $0.50 per page from microfilm. Copies generally must be provided within 15 days, with inspection permitted within five working days.


Prelitigation attorney requests fall under Evidence Code § 1158. When an attorney presents a qualifying signed authorization, records must be made available for inspection and copying within five days, under that section's own fee rules: $0.10 per page for standard reproduction, $0.20 per page from microfilm, plus specified clerical costs, postage, and other actual costs.


HIPAA's individual right of access is a third framework, with a 30 calendar day outer limit subject to one qualifying extension.


Electronic delivery can reduce copying and mailing costs, and reasonable media costs may apply for portable media. Confirm the pathway before quoting a timeline or budget.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can I request medical records for a deceased family member in a wrongful death claim?**


Yes, but the documentation depends on the legal basis for authority. HIPAA recognizes an executor, an administrator, or another person authorized under applicable law to act for the decedent or estate. Evidence Code § 1158 also contemplates authorization by the personal representative or an heir for qualifying prelitigation attorney access. Letters testamentary or letters of administration plus a death certificate are commonly requested but not universally required, and facility policies vary. Confirm what the facility needs.


### **Are there specific rules for requesting psychiatric or mental health records in California?**


For a prelitigation attorney request, the statutory form in Evidence Code § 1158 separately identifies mental health records, so make that selection explicitly. A generic authorization that does not address them may be rejected. Additional confidentiality laws can apply depending on the provider and record type, and dedicated psychiatric providers often scrutinize authorizations more closely.


### **What should I do if a Long Beach provider refuses to release records?**


Confirm your authorization is complete and specifically covers the records requested, then ask for a written explanation. One distinction matters: when an individual's HIPAA right-of-access request is denied, the covered entity must give a written denial with the basis and complaint information, and the Office for Civil Rights is the complaint route. A denial of an attorney authorization request is not governed by that rule, and the appropriate agency depends on the provider and legal basis. Where a denial appears improper, a subpoena duces tecum or motion to compel may be the practical path.


### **How do I obtain imaging studies on disc?**


Imaging usually requires a request separate from general records. On the authorization, explicitly request diagnostic imaging on CD or DVD, or radiology images in digital format. Reasonable allowable media costs may apply. If imaging does not arrive with the records, contact radiology directly, since some facilities run it through a separate workflow. Specify DICOM format if your experts need it.


### **What is the difference between a HIPAA authorization and a general release of information?**


A HIPAA authorization satisfies the Privacy Rule's requirements for disclosing protected health information: a meaningful description of the information, the disclosing party, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration, a signature and date, and the required notices. A general release may not meet all of those and can be rejected. For PI requests in California, use the facility's own form or an authorization substantially in the § 1158 statutory form, which providers are directed to accept when valid and properly completed.
